fi-ecsenius-bicolor.title: Bicolor Blenny
fi-ecsenius-bicolor.summary: A personable perching blenny, blue-brown in front and orange behind. Grazes algae on the rocks.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 11 cm (4.3 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Usually fine, but an underfed fish may nip clam mantles or fleshy LPS
Herbivore. Feed algae-based frozen and dried foods; it also grazes algae in the tank
Indo-Pacific: Maldives to the Phoenix Islands, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to the southern Great Barrier Reef; throughout Micronesia
notes: Needs rocks to perch on and holes to hide in; in the wild it lives in empty worm tubes.
May pick on other blennies, small gobies and dartfish.

fi-salarias-fasciatus.title: Lawnmower Blenny
fi-salarias-fasciatus.summary: A peaceful, comical algae grazer with big eyes and a mottled tan body. Also sold as the Sailfin or Algae Blenny.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly unless a mated pair in a larger tank
Listed reef compatible, but known to nip small-polyp stony corals and clam mantles
Herbivore. Grazes microalgae; supplement with vegetable matter, spirulina and herbivore foods
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia
notes: Does best in an established tank with lots of natural algae and rockwork.
Lives on shallow reef flats in the wild, even brackish edges.

fi-ophioblennius-atlanticus.title: Redlip Blenny
fi-ophioblennius-atlanticus.summary: A Caribbean blenny with a blunt "horse face", red lips and dark body. Spends its time hopping between rocks grazing.
rows: About 5 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 19 cm (7.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly unless a mated pair in a larger tank
Listed reef compatible, but may nip small-polyp stony corals and clam mantles
Herbivore. Needs plenty of natural microalgae; supplement with algae foods
Atlantic Ocean: oceanic islands and along the coast of west Africa from Senegal to Angola
notes: Aggressive mainly toward fish shaped like itself.
warn: Has long, sharp canine teeth and can bite hard (FishBase rates it traumatogenic).
